questions.prompt: Complete: "The student ___ won the prize is in my class."
questions.explanation: "The student" is a person, so the relative pronoun is "who" (or "that"): the student who won the prize. "Which" refers only to things, and "what" and "when" never follow a noun to define a person.

questions.prompt: Complete: "We want to plant trees ___ will make our school green."
questions.explanation: "Trees" are things, so the relative pronoun is "which" (or "that"): trees which will make our school green. "Which they" gives "will make" two subjects, "who" is only for people, and "what" cannot follow a noun as a relative pronoun.
"Fast" is a short adjective, so it takes -er, and "than" introduces the lion: faster than. "More" is only for long adjectives, "fastest" is the superlative, and "as … than" mixes two structures.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Mount Chambi is ___ mountain in Tunisia." (high)
questions.explanation: Chambi is compared with all the mountains of Tunisia, so we need the superlative: "high" is short, so the highest (1,544 m, the top of the country). "The higher" is a comparative, and "the most" is only for long adjectives.

options.text: She is as taller as her sister.
She is as tall as her sister.
She is tall as her sister.
She is as tall than her sister.

questions.explanation: Equality is as + plain adjective + as: as tall as. "As taller as" puts a comparative inside the structure, the sentence without the first "as" is incomplete, and "than" never closes an equality.

questions.prompt: Join the two sentences: "Factories release fumes. The fumes pollute the air."

options.text: Factories release fumes who pollute the air.
Factories release fumes which they pollute the air.
Factories release fumes which pollute the air.
Factories release fumes what pollute the air.

questions.explanation: "The fumes" is the subject of the second sentence and a thing, so "which" replaces it: fumes which pollute the air. Adding "they" gives the verb two subjects, "who" is only for people, and "what" never follows a noun to define it.
